intro: A Shopify store looks more polished when every product photo feels like part of one coordinated shoot. Mixed backgrounds and odd crops make a collection page look unfinished, even when the products themselves are great. AIVideosUGC helps you even things out: upload the photos you have, choose a clean background or describe a setting, and get square images that sit neatly side by side.

Product pages also need something that keeps shoppers scrolling. Build a three-image product-page set with a main view, one detail and one scene, reuse the square treatment for collection tiles, and make a separate seasonal set when a launch changes the background or color. Everything stays private in your account until you download it and add it in your Shopify admin.
tips: Use a consistent shape for every product photo in a collection so the grid lines up neatly.
Put your clearest, simplest photo first, because it's usually the one shown on collection pages.
Write short alt text for each image so shoppers using screen readers know what's pictured.

faq.q: What size should Shopify product photos be?
faq.a: Shopify says square 2048×2048 images usually display best. Pair product photos with a consistent background and camera height, then check how your storefront displays the image. See [Shopify's product media guidance](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/product-media/product-media-types).

faq.q: Can I add a video to my Shopify product page?
faq.a: Yes. Shopify product media supports video; check the file duration, size, resolution and format against Shopify's current product-media guidance, then upload it in the product's media section.

faq.q: Will all my product photos look consistent?
faq.a: Describing a consistent background each time helps a lot. Results can still vary slightly, so review each image before it goes on your store.

faq.q: What are Shopify product video limits?
faq.a: Shopify allows product videos up to 10 minutes, 1 GB and 4K (4096×2160) in MP4, MOV or WebM. Our generator offers 6, 10, 15 or 30-second clips in five shapes; preview how the file appears in your storefront.

faq.q: How do I keep collection images consistent?
faq.a: Use a repeatable camera height, square framing and a related background treatment, then compare every new image beside the existing collection before publishing.

faq.q: Should social crops go in the product gallery?
faq.a: Keep square product-page images together in the gallery and make a separate 9:16 asset for Stories or Reels so a tall crop does not force the product grid out of shape.

faq.q: Do I need to reshoot older products to match?
faq.a: No. Upload the photo you already have for each item and the same background treatment is applied, so older products can match new arrivals without another shoot.

faq.q: Can I use the photos and clips on my store?
faq.a: Yes. Downloaded files are yours to publish in Shopify and carry no AIVideosUGC watermark, so they fit straight into your product and collection pages.

overview.h2: Make a catalog feel like one store
overview.d: Shopify collection pages are easier to scan when product photos share a shape, background family, and camera height. Use square images for the product page, collection or home card, and social feed post around this product.

overview.h2: Choose media for the page job
overview.d: Shopify says square 2048×2048 product images usually display best; its image limit is 5000×5000 pixels or 25 MP and under 20 MB. Product videos can be up to 10 minutes and 1 GB, up to 4K (4096×2160), in MP4, MOV or WebM. AIVideosUGC offers 6, 10 or 15-second clips in five shapes—9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3 and 3:4—with the cost shown before the job starts. Your storefront controls how media appears. Check [Shopify's product media types](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/product-media/product-media-types) for current upload details.

overview.h2: Build a collection that scans cleanly
overview.d: Use one repeatable square treatment across collection cards: a similar camera height, background family, and margin around the product. A bowl set can show the same glaze colors from a low angle, a lunch container can show its open compartments, and a skincare tube can show a clean routine. Keep the product name and price in Shopify admin rather than burning them into the image.

A product-page gallery answers detail questions, a collection card needs a quick silhouette, and a social post can show use in context. Start separate jobs when the crop or action changes. Shopify supports product media video under its own duration, size, resolution, and file rules; AIVideosUGC clip length is a separate generator choice, so preview the downloaded file against the destination before uploading.

overview.h2: Keep the catalog consistent as it grows
overview.d: Review a new square image beside the existing collection before publishing. Check the item is the same color and variant, the background does not compete with the product, and the crop leaves room for the Shopify card layout. Make a distinct lifestyle or social asset when a tall crop would make the collection grid uneven, then keep the square gallery intact.

overview.h2: Assign a set to each Shopify surface
overview.d: Use the product-page set for a main view, a detail and a scene; use a single square collection tile for quick grid scanning; and make a seasonal set when several products need the same launch treatment. Keep social crops as separate assets and review each file in the intended Shopify surface before publishing.

items.d: Photograph each item from a comparable front or three-quarter angle so the collection grid does not jump from product to product.
Reuse a short description such as matte stone, warm daylight, and soft shadow, then change only the product and action.
Include handles, cords, lids, and the base in the source. A consistent crop cannot repair a missing component.

scene_recipes.h2: Scenes for collection and product pages

items.d: Place three candle vessels on one pale wood surface with matching daylight and enough space for each label to be reviewed later.
Drape a throw blanket over a reading chair with the full weave visible and one corner falling naturally toward the floor.
A water bottle slides into an open gym bag beside a towel, then reappears on a bench for a close look.
Show a planter on a sunny sill with the pot and leaves fully in frame, leaving room for a real size note later.

after_download.h2: Load the files into Shopify with a final check

items.d: Confirm the image dimensions and file size, or the video duration, container, size, and resolution, against Shopify's current product-media guidance.
Add product names, descriptions, and alt text yourself; AI-generated lettering is not a reliable source for product descriptions or labels.
View the new image beside the rest of the collection and adjust the crop or background when one item looks out of place.
Keep a 9:16 clip for Stories or Reels as a separate asset instead of forcing a tall crop into the product gallery.
